findings.evidence: Never rebase onto local `main` (often stale, so the branch lands on an old base), never `git pull` (...), never `git merge` (...)
findings.fix: Remove this restatement. Step 3 (line 19) already says "Rebase onto the remote ref, never local `main`; never `git pull` or `git merge`". Move the three short reasons into that line so the rule appears once.

findings.evidence: Step 2 puts the fetch, the remote-ancestry check with `git cherry`, the ownership question and the merge-commit question in one run of dense bullets, and step 3 (lines 20-22) packs three conditional rebase forms into prose
findings.fix: Split step 2 into ordered checks, each with a single outcome: fetch, remote ahead, ownership, merge commits. Write step 3(c) as a three-row decision table (condition, then the rebase command) so each branch can be scanned and followed without re-reading the paragraph.

findings.evidence: The Gotchas section has three bullets, and two of them (lines 28-29) repeat rules already stated in steps 3 and 5
findings.fix: Replace the duplicated rules with facts the body does not cover. Example: with `rebase.updateRefs=true` in the user's config, `git rebase` also moves other local branches stacked on this one. Those branches are not pushed, so list them with `git branch --contains "$orig"` and report them.

findings.evidence: If the fork range is shorter, ask "fork-point would drop N commits; use the plain merge-base rebase instead, or stop?"
findings.fix: `--fork-point` always returns a commit at least as recent as the plain merge-base. So whenever `fork` differs from `plain`, the fork range is shorter, the question always fires, and the `git rebase --onto "$base/$target" "$fork" "$branch"` form in step 3(c) can never run. It also labels the legitimate case (old upstream commits rewritten by a force-push or squash-merge) as dropped feature work. Before asking, list the dropped commits with `git log --oneline "$plain..$fork"`. Ask only when some of them are not in `$base/$target` by patch, checked with `git cherry "$base/$target" "$fork" "$plain"` showing `+` lines. Otherwise use the `--onto "$fork"` form.
